purpose: Carvedilol is used to treat heart failure and high blood pressure. It can also be used after a heart attack to help protect your heart. By keeping your heart working more efficiently, it can help you feel less short of breath and more able to do everyday activities.
how_it_works: Carvedilol works by blocking certain signals in your body that would otherwise make your heart beat faster and harder. Think of it like taking your heart off of overdrive — it helps your heart beat more slowly and with less effort. It also relaxes your blood vessels so your heart does not have to pump as hard to push blood through your body.
common_side_effects: You may feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when you stand up quickly — so take your time getting up. Tiredness or low energy is also common, particularly when you first start the medication. Some people notice slow heartbeat, low blood pressure, or mild weight gain from fluid retention.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor — stopping abruptly can cause serious heart problems. Tell your doctor if you have asthma or breathing problems, as this medication can sometimes make breathing worse. Also let your doctor know if you have diabetes, since carvedilol can hide some signs of low blood sugar.
typical_dosing: For heart failure, the usual starting dose is 3.125 mg taken twice a day with food. For high blood pressure, it is often started at 6.25 mg twice daily. Your doctor will slowly increase your dose over time based on how you are doing — always take it exactly as prescribed and with a meal to reduce dizziness.
